solutions.text: The given sum counts the number of non-decreasing 61-tuples of integers \(\left(n_{0}, \ldots, n_{60}\right)\) from the set \(\{0,1,2\}\). Such 61-tuples are in one-to-one correspondence with strictly increasing 61 -tuples of integers \(\left(m_{0}, \ldots, m_{60}\right)\) from the set \(\{0,1,2, \ldots, 62\}\) : simply let \(m_{k}=n_{k}+k\). But the number of such \(\left(m_{0}, \ldots, m_{60}\right)\) is almost by definition \(\binom{63}{61}=\binom{63}{2}=1953\).
